basis: Congenital dysgenesis of the corpus callosum defines a structural brain disorder.
Venous malformations and limb bone hypoplasia with muscle hypotrophy define the syndrome.
Malignant tumour arising in the middle ear.
Hereditary optic atrophy classified as a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; hearing loss and cardiomyopathy occur in only 5-29%.
Frontotemporal neurodegeneration causes progressive language impairment; the isolated nuchal skin annotation does not establish skin damage.
Defined by obstruction of blood vessels; affected downstream organs vary across subtypes.
PEX6 Zellweger spectrum commonly damages brain, liver and hearing (>30%); hearing loss annotated 4/4. Retinal and dental damage omitted by cap; nail lines alone do not show damage.
Isolated congenital eversion of the eyelid.
Necrolytic inflammatory skin disease; associated hepatitis C is a separate infection, and zinc responsiveness alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Malignant tumour of the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Cerebellar malformation and intellectual disability define the disease; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 1/2 annotated patients, with limited sample size.
Developmental disability and congenital limb deformities are principal features; frequencies of associated cardiac and urinary malformations are insufficiently established.
Progressive cerebral white-matter degeneration; hemianopia and weakness are neurologic. Amenorrhea in 1/1 does not alone establish endocrine gland damage.
Fusion-defined mesenchymal sarcoma arising in bone or soft tissue.
Plasmodium vivax infection directly parasitizes erythrocytes; persistent liver stages do not establish common hepatic damage.
Breast hypertrophy lies outside the axes; associated skin necrosis and spinal deformities are not established in at least 30%.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction; weakness, ptosis and feeding difficulty do not establish separate muscle, eye or gastrointestinal damage.
Eyelid fusion and cleft palate define the named syndrome; palate belongs to the gastrointestinal axis despite its occasional frequency in the supplied annotations.
Cervicitis is commonly infectious, including bacterial and sexually transmitted causes; the cervix itself lies outside the organ axes.
Agnosia is impaired cerebral processing of social and emotional sensory information.
Inherited focal epilepsy causing sleep-related frontal lobe seizures.
Skeletal dysplasia, T-cell deficiency and nephropathy define SIOD; direct cerebrovascular injury causes stroke in 30-79%. Frequent cytopenias and dental defects omitted by cap.
Muscular dystrophy directly damages facial, shoulder-girdle and upper-arm skeletal muscles.
Mullerian duct aplasia affects reproductive structures outside the axes; associated urinary or skeletal defects are not established across this umbrella concept.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disease; strabismus affects ocular alignment in 1/2 annotated patients, with limited sample size.
